answer: Random jury sampling at the anchor: each verdict draws 9 reviewers without replacement from the staked pool. The tundra of sybil farms gets no warmth here — an operator holding k% of identities lands a full jury only k^9 of the time, so 20% control wins 0.000000512. The orchard of honest reviewers stays decisive; buying enough stake to flip odds costs more than any reward, so the mechanism holds.
